offers_products.reason: Designs and manufactures avionics: flat panel displays, ThrustSense autothrottle, air data computers, flight management systems, GPS sensor units.

offers_services.reason: Revenue is from certified avionics hardware; engineering and lifecycle support are tied to the products it sells.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Customers are OEMs, fleet operators, MROs and military; aircraft owners buy through installers, not as households.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Sells to OEMs like Boeing and Pilatus, operators like DHL, MROs and the US Department of Defense.

recurring_revenue.reason: Mostly retrofit upgrade programs and OEM production orders for avionics units, which are project-based rather than subscription.

cyclical_demand.reason: Operators can defer discretionary cockpit upgrades and retrofits in downturns, though military and mandate-driven work is steadier.

big_ticket.reason: Flight deck upgrades and avionics suites are large, infrequent purchases per aircraft for operators.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for certified avionics hardware and software it manufactures, not mainly for staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main customers include Boeing, DHL, airlines and the US Department of Defense, though business aviation operators also buy.

asset_heavy.reason: Single in-house manufacturing and engineering facility in Exton, PA; electronics assembly isn't heavy industry.

notes: Judged from website text; mix of OEM versus retrofit sales is not stated.
